    #CA1 S1 (2024 - 2025)

    #Question 1

    A load with an impedance of 48+j36 Ω/phase is connected to a 3-phase,
    440V     Δ-connected system. Determine the apparent power of the load.

    Conversion of load impedance,

    ZY​=3ZΔ​​=348+j36​

    ZY​=16+j12

    ZY​=20∠36.87° Ω

    Phase voltage,

    VP​=3​VL​​=3​440​=254.03 V

    Phase current,

    IˉP​=ZˉY​VˉP​​=20∠36.87°254.03∠0°​

    IˉP​=12.702∠−36.87° A

    Complex (apparent) power,

    Sˉ=3VˉP​IˉP​∗

    Sˉ=3(254.03∠0°×12.702∠36.87°)

    Sˉ=9680∠36.87° VA

    #Question 2

    Two wattmeters are connected to a 3-phase system. Their readings are
    90 kW and 60 kW respectively. Determine the power factor of the system.

    Power factor angle,

    φ=tan−1[P1​+P2​3​(P1​−P2​)​]

    φ=tan−1[90+603​(90−60)​]

    φ=19.107°

    Power factor,

    PF=cosφ=cos19.107°=0.94491

    #Question 3

    A capacitor bank of rating 8 kVAr is connected in parallel to a load in a 3-phase,
    440V     Δ-connected system. The load has an impedance of 22∠30°Ω/phase.
    Determine the apparent power and power factor of the system.

    Conversion of load impedance,

    ZY​=3ZΔ​​=322∠30°​=322​∠30° Ω

    Phase voltage,

    VP​=3VL​​=3440​=254.03 V

    Reactance of capacitor bank,

    QC​=−3IP​2XC​=−XC​3VP​2​

    −8000=−XC​3(524.03)2​

    XC​=24.2 Ω

    Impedance of capacitor bank,

    ZC​=0−j24.2=24.2∠−90° Ω

    Equivalent impedance,

    Zˉeq​1​=ZˉY​1​+ZˉC​1​

    Zˉeq​1​=223​∠−30°+24.21​∠90°

    Zˉeq​1​=0.11809−j0.02686

    Zˉeq​1​=0.12111∠−12.814°

    Zˉeq​=8.257∠12.814° Ω

    Phase current,

    IˉP​=Zˉeq​VˉP​​=8.257∠12.814°254.03∠0°​

    IˉP​=30.765∠−12.814°

    Complex power,

    Sˉ=3VˉP​IP​∗

    Sˉ=3(254.03∠0°×30.765∠12.814°)

    Sˉ=23446∠12.814° VA

    Power factor,

    PF=cosφ

    PF=cos12.814

    PF=0.9751

    #CA2 S1 (2024 - 2025)

    #Question 1 + 2 + 3

    The parameters of a 20kVA 4000V/200V step-down transformer are to be determined.
    An open circuit test is performed on the low-voltage side.
    A short circuit test is performed on the high-voltage side.

    Open circuit test: VOC​=150 V, IOC​=3 A, POC​=200 W

    Short circuit test: VSC​=50 V, ISC​=4.8 A, PSC​=80 W

    Determine RC​ and XM​ referred to the primary side (4000V).

    For open circuit test, measurements are done on the low-voltage side.
    Thus, the values for RC​ and XM​ correspond to the low-voltage side.
    The low-voltage side is the secondary in a step-down transformer.

    Core resistance,

    RC,S​=POC​VOC​2​=2001502​=112.5 Ω

    Current through core resistance,

    IRC,S​​=RC,S​VOC​​=112.5150​=1.3333 A

    Current through magnetizing impedance,

    IOC​=IRC,S​​2+IXM,S​​2​

    3=1.33332+IXM,S​​2​

    IXM,S​​=2.6874 A

    Magnetizing impedance,

    XM,S​=IXM,S​​VOC​​=2.6874150​=55.816 Ω

    Referring to the primary side,

    RC,P​=a2RC,S​=202(112.5)=45 kΩ

    XM,P​=a2XM,S​=202(55.816)=22.326 kΩ

    Determine Req​ and Xeq​ referred to the primary side (4000V).

    For short circuit test, measurements are done on the high-voltage side.
    Thus, the values for Req​ and Xeq​ correspond to the high-voltage side.
    The high-voltage side is the primary in the step-down transformer.

    Equivalent resistance of the coils,

    Req,P​=ISC​2PSC​​=4.8280​=3.4722 Ω

    Equivalent impedance of the coils,

    Zeq,P​=ISC​VSC​​=4.850​=10.417 Ω

    Equivalent reactance of the coils,

    Zeq,P​=Req,P​2+Xeq,P​2​

    10.417=3.47222+Xeq,P​2​

    Xeq,P​=9.8209 Ω

    Determine the voltage regulation for a lagging power factor of 0.8.

    Current through secondary side,

    SˉS​=VˉS​IˉS​∠φ

    IˉS​=20020×103​∠−cos−10.8

    IˉS​=100∠−36.87° A

    Equivalent impedance of the coils referred to secondary side,

    Zˉeq,S​=a2Zˉeq,P​​=20210.417∠70.529°​=0.0260425∠70.529° Ω

    No load voltage,

    VˉS,nl​=VˉS​+IˉS​Zˉeq,S​

    VˉS,nl​=200∠0°+(100∠−36.87°)(0.0260425∠70.529°)

    VˉS,nl​=200∠0°+2.60425∠33.549°

    VˉS,nl​=202.17+j1.4392

    VˉS,nl​=202.18∠0.40787° V

    Voltage regulation,

    VR=VS,fl​VS,nl​−VS,fl​​=200202.18−200​=1.09%

    #Question 4

    A four-pole 50Hz induction motor rotates at a speed of 1420rpm.
    Determine the slip of the motor.

    Synchronous speed,

    nsync​=p120fs​​=4120(50)​

    nsync​=1500 rev/min

    Slip of the motor,

    s=nsync​nsync​−nmech​​

    s=15001500−1420​

    s=5.3333%

    #Question 5

    A six-pole 60Hz induction motor rotates at a speed of 1140rpm.
    The air-gap power of the motor is 6kW.
    Determine the developed power.

    Synchronous speed,

    nsync​=p120fs​​=6120(60)​

    nsync​=1200 rev/min

    Slip of the motor,

    s=nsync​nsync​−nmech​​

    s=12001200−1140​

    s=0.05

    Converted/developed power,

    Pconv​=PAG​−PRCL​

    Pconv​=3I2​2sR2​​−3I2​2R2​

    Pconv​=3I2​2R2​(s1​−1)

    Pconv​=3I2​2R2​(s1−s​)

    Pconv​=(1−s)PAG​

    Pconv​=(1−0.05)(6000)

    Pconv​=5700 W

    #Part (d)

    Power factor can be improved by connecting a capacitor bank parallel to the load.
    Capacitor only alters reactive power of the load, active power remains unchanged.

    Active power of load,

    P=38.751cos32.388°=32.723 kW

    Reactive power of load (before adding capacitor),

    Qold​=38.751sin32.388°=20.757 kVAR

    Desired power factor angle,

    PF=cosφ

    φ=cos−10.99

    φ=8.1096°

    Reactive power of load (after adding capacitor),

    tanφ=PQnew​​

    Qnew​=32.723tan8.1096°

    Qnew​=4.71 kVAR

    Required capacitor rating,

    QC​=Qnew​−Qold​

    QC​=4.71−20.757

    QC​=−16.047 kVAR

    #Part (d)

    Coil is connected to a 48V source and supplied with a constant current.

    Let x denote the airgap distance.

    Total reluctance of circuit,

    Rtot​=μ0​A1​x​+2μ0​A2​x​

    Rtot​=[(4π×10−7)(0.1×0.1)1​+2(4π×10−7)(0.05×0.1)1​]x

    Rtot​=(159.15×106)x

    Magnetic energy stored in field,

    Wf​=21​i2L=21​i2N2R1​

    Note that φ changes as x changes when the part moves.
    Therefore, we cannot use the equation     Wf​=21​φ2Rtot​.

    Magnetic force acting on steel bar,

    F=dxdWf​​=21​i2N2dxd​Rtot​1​

    F=21​(24)2(2000)2[−(159.15×106)x21​]

    F=−x27.2382​

    Magnitude of force when x=0.02 m,

    F=0.0227.2382​=18096 N

    Power factor can be improved by connecting a capacitor bank parallel to the load.
